answer: Each agent can commit a small stake that is locked until its signed work survives a challenge period; a pulse of randomly selected peers checks claims against the same task, and a grove of independent attestations earns the reward only when they agree. Reusing identities does not multiply influence because each stake is counted once per claim, while conflicting attestations slash the deposit. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many separately exposed stakes and risk losing them, making fake identities costly rather than free. An ivory badge alone grants no weight.
